A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MAETok research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete Appendices A–C are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original tokenizer reconstruction, ImageNet generation, latent-space analysis and ablation results in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds component, token and positional-encoding ablations, alternative guidance results and MAETok + USiT-2B evaluation.

M1.justification: The MAETok architecture, objectives, masking procedure and decoder fine-tuning in Section 3 are unchanged. Section 4.5 newly applies Autoguidance using earlier generator checkpoints and guidance-free training, introducing limited downstream generation-procedure variants.

E1.justification: Both versions use ImageNet at 256 and 512 resolution, LAION-COCO tokenizer training, and ImageNet/MS-COCO reconstruction evaluation. Conditional and unconditional generation are already present in v1. The added experiments retain this dataset and task coverage.

E2.justification: v1 discusses advanced guidance as future work; v2 reports evaluations of Autoguidance and guidance-free training alongside standard CFG in Section 4.5. The external baseline sets in the main generation and reconstruction tables are retained; MAETok + USiT-2B is an additional proposed-system configuration.

E3.justification: v2 adds evaluation with a 2B-parameter USiT generator, alternative guidance procedures, component-removal controls, 128-versus-256-token configurations and an APE/RoPE comparison under mixed-resolution training. Existing benchmark metrics and training-configuration tables remain unchanged. Appendix B.3 documents the existing GMM experiment rather than establishing a revised protocol.

E4.justification: New Table 6 systematically combines and removes masking, learnable tokens and auxiliary decoders. Appendix C.4/Table 13 additionally tests token type/count and positional encoding across resolutions, while Section 4.5 evaluates guidance alternatives. These substantially extend design validation beyond v1's existing masking, reconstruction-target, mask-ratio and decoder-depth studies.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added results retain the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 substantially expands reported evidence through the new ablations and generation configurations. Table 3 adds MAETok + USiT-2B gFID of 1.72 without CFG and 1.65 with CFG. Section 4.5 reports 1.54 with Autoguidance and 1.51 with guidance-free training. Table 13 adds token-count and RoPE results, including 512-resolution rFID of 1.43 for APE versus 0.72 for RoPE. Existing corresponding scores are retained; these are additional configurations, not revised same-setting results.

T1.justification: The GMM definitions, Theorem 2.1, Appendix A assumptions, theorems and derivations are unchanged. The added similar-decoder-capacity qualification appears in the empirical motivation and does not revise the formal mathematical analysis.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements and conclusion retain the same substantive claims: discriminative latent structure supports diffusion learning, variational regularization is unnecessary, and MAETok enables efficient, competitive ImageNet generation using 128 tokens. Added experiments supply support without redefining these contributions.

C2.justification: Section 2 newly qualifies the generation-quality argument by assuming similar tokenizer-decoder capacity. Sections 4.5 and C.4 add interpretations about complementary component benefits, 128-token sufficiency and RoPE's resolution generalization. However, the new assertion that removing learnable tokens is most harmful conflicts with Table 6, where removing the auxiliary decoder produces worse reconstruction and generation scores.

D1.justification: New Appendix B.3 documents GMM latent flattening, PCA retaining over 90% explained variance, standardization, matched dimensions, ImageNet fitting, batch size, hardware and fitting times. It also specifies the optimizer and schedule for Figure 2's SiT-L experiment. These are useful disclosures for existing analyses; the original training tables and code/model access information are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Chen et al. (2025) on guidance-free generation, Qiu et al. (2025) on robust latents, and Zhao and Schwing (2025) on guidance. These extend the guidance discussion and latent-diffusion references without substantially changing the paper's research positioning.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section sequence are retained. Changes include localized clarification in Section 2, expanded Section 4.5, new Appendices B.3 and C.4, renumbering the qualitative-results subsection, minor wording corrections, revised affiliations and acknowledgments.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 6 and 13, expands Table 3 with a USiT-2B row, and renumbers subsequent tables. Appendix tables, Figure 9 and generation montages are relocated through reflow. Existing figures and sample images are retained without substantive visual replacement.

improvement.justification: v1 lacked the GMM preprocessing details and dedicated token/RoPE tests that v2 supplies in Appendices B.3 and C.4. These improve reproducibility and strengthen support for existing design choices. The gain is limited by sparse documentation of the new generation variants and the incorrect component-importance interpretation accompanying Table 6, but the added transparency and controlled evidence provide a modest net improvement.
